blocks.text: This chapter’s priestly, Levitical, and city registers belong to the opening genealogies of 1 Chronicles. Together, those registers connect the restored community with Israel’s tribes, David, priestly and Levitical lines, and preexilic Jerusalem. The chapter’s lists therefore place its attention on kinship, office, and communal continuity, not simply on individual names.

Across the surrounding genealogies, these records function as selective literary maps of kinship, land, office, and restored identity rather than as exhaustive modern-style biological pedigrees. Repeated lines, gaps, and variant names should therefore be considered case by case rather than assumed to follow one uniform pattern.
